critical.issue: P1-D REGEX-INJECTION MISS. server.py hr_employee_roster (~L4785-4793) builds Mongo $regex directly from user query params `q`, `role`, `department` WITHOUT re.escape(). Payload q=[[[[[ raises pymongo.errors.OperationFailure 'Regular expression is invalid: missing terminating ] for character class' → HTTP 500. Repro: `curl -H 'X-Admin-Token: …' 'BASE/api/hr/employee-roster?q=%5B%5B%5B%5B%5B'` returns 500 Internal Server Error. Same file was NOT listed in the sweep-scope (sweep hit hr_portal.py but roster is defined inline in server.py). Fix: wrap the three `$regex` sites at server.py lines 4786, 4788, 4791 with re.escape(). Payloads (a+b)*, .*, ^$, (?:.*)+ ALL return 200 correctly — only unterminated character-class metachar (`[[[[[`) crashes, which confirms the surface: raw user input → Mongo regex compiler → 500.

rca of the issue: RCA: The P1-D sweep was file-scoped (as reported in the review request: pm_engine.py, equipment.py, master_history.py, employee_lifecycle.py, employee_requests.py, hr_portal.py). But `/api/hr/employee-roster` is declared inline in server.py, not in hr_portal.py — so the sweep never touched it. Any string coming in through the `q`, `role`, or `department` query parameters is interpolated straight into a MongoDB `$regex` document. When the payload contains a syntactically invalid regex fragment (e.g. `[[[[[`, an unterminated character class), Mongo's regex compiler rejects the query with OperationFailure 51091, which surfaces as an unhandled 500 in the FastAPI handler. Reproduction: 1) POST /api/auth/multi-login → grab portal_tokens.admin. 2) GET /api/hr/employee-roster?q=[[[[[ with `X-Admin-Token: <token>`. 3) Observe HTTP 500 + backend log `pymongo.errors.OperationFailure: Regular expression is invalid: missing terminating ] for character class`. Mitigation: wrap all three raw-user-input regex sites with `re.escape(value)` (or a shared helper `_safe_needle(v)` used across the sweep), and add /api/hr/employee-roster to the sweep's assertion set. This is a defensive fix, not a security disclosure — the endpoint is auth-gated — but a hostile authenticated actor could DoS the API worker with tight ReDoS payloads today. Estimated fix: 5 lines. Blast radius after fix: none (pure literal search).
